result.summary: Do not ship: expanded HTTP error logging exposes URL credentials even at WARNING level.

findings.title: HTTP error logging exposes reverse-proxy passwords
findings.body: Confirmed with the accepted URL `http://alice:proxy-password@localhost:7878` and a mocked 502: validate_connection logs the plaintext password. HTTPX includes the request URL in the exception; collect_secrets() in startup.py collects API keys and application auth secrets, but not URL passwords, so both logging sinks retain it. With logging configured to WARNING, the existing INFO startup banner is suppressed; this change newly exposes credentials in that configuration. The previous status-only warning avoided this disclosure.
findings.recommendation: Keep the status-only warning, or explicitly remove credentials and sensitive URL components before logging. Add a regression test using a credential-bearing URL, a 502 response, and WARNING-level logging.

next_steps: Remove credential-bearing exception text from the warning and verify redaction in both logging sinks.
